## Short arrival, departure and car enquiries on 12 November

<a id="short-arrival-departure-and-car-enquiries-on-november-12"></a>

**Sources on this page:** p183 A, p183 B, p183 C, p183 E.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov12-arrival-departure-and-car-short-arrival-departure-and-car-enquiries-on-november-12"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Four short native records report arrival and departure, request an arrival notification, and enquire about a car. The arrival enquiry and departure text have earlier p174 parallels already published in this repository; the new witnesses add source support to those readings. In particular, the two complementary arrival-enquiry witnesses now supply every coordinate and every plaintext pair without changing an observed coordinate under the conservative glyph masks. The previously catalogued witnesses are not counted again.

<a id="source-p183-a"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov12-arrival-departure-and-car-p183-a"></a>

### p183 A

**Source transcription — header:** `A) CZ v CM (20.00 p.m., November 12th); 20.00; RIZI-64`

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
GUTANGEKOMMENXISTDORTWASLOSXSEIF
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the unchanged raw output:**

> Gut angekommen. Ist dort was los. SEIF.

**Meaning:** The sender reports having arrived safely and asks whether anything is happening at the other end. The closing SEIF is retained as an abbreviated label; this short message does not itself give a location or establish a full personal identity.

**Editorial limits:**

- All 64 native coordinates decode directly under the unchanged key, with no changes or source-mask fills. The following NF CM UM transmission-control text is outside the 64-coordinate body.
- The wording IST DORT WAS LOS is a question. The readable quotation uses a period so that a question mark remains reserved for an unresolved plaintext position in this edition.
- SEIF is not expanded to a full name in the exact readable quotation.

<a id="source-p183-b"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov12-arrival-departure-and-car-p183-b"></a>

### p183 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) CM v CZ (18.54 p.m., November 12th); 19.10; RIZI-74`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
WENN??IFERTE?NGETROF?ENBITTE?ACHR?TO?
```

**Edited output — 0 observed-coordinate substitutions and 8 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
WENNSEIFERTEINGETROFFENBITTENACHRXTOF
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Wenn Seifert eingetroffen, bitte NACHR. TOF.

**Meaning:** The message asks for notification when Seifert has arrived. NACHR is read as an abbreviated request for news or a message. TOF remains a closing label with no claimed personal or station identity.

**Editorial limits:**

- The native body contains 74 occupied slots, including literal Z at source indices 4 and 31, W at 42, and five B glyphs at 60–64. These eight invalid coordinate glyphs remain in the transcription and become eight separately priced analysis-mask fills.
- The proposal changes no observed ADFGVX coordinate. The five B-shaped slots are filled with D coordinates; this is an explicit source-mask completion, not a silent claim that five clearly printed Ds were present.
- The source ending CZ UM is transmission control after the 74-slot ciphertext and is excluded from the body on that printed framing.
- NACHR and TOF remain abbreviated or literal; no sender biography is supplied.
- The earlier p174 B witness supplies all eight invalid-glyph values here, while this source supplies D at p174 source 20, supporting its previously unresolved N in EINGETROFFEN. Under conservative masks all 74 source coordinates and all 37 target pairs have an observed witness, with zero observed-coordinate conflicts.
- If the earlier C/G-like glyph is instead treated as an observed G, the complete-word proposal costs one observed substitution in that alternative. The new D witness does not change the appearance of the old glyph.

### p183 C

**Source transcription — header:** `C) CM v CZ (17.26 p.m., November 12th); 18.20; RIZI-46`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
SQIFERTABGEFAHRENXRENTE
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
SEIFERTABGEFAHRENXRENTE
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> Seifert abgefahren. RENTE.

**Meaning:** The proposed reading reports that Seifert has departed. RENTE is the literal closing field; the record alone does not identify it as a particular person or station.

**Editorial limits:**

- All 46 printed coordinates are retained, including the final six FFVDD V omitted from the earlier OCR body. The following CZ is outside the ciphertext.
- The source produces SQIFERT directly. The proposal SEIFERT changes one observed coordinate; the neighboring arrival enquiry supports the name but does not make this change free.
- The full 46-slot ciphertext is preserved; no historical prefix or suffix is invented.
- Compared with existing p174 E, this source supports E at plaintext 4 through observed source 2 X instead of G. Both witnesses still have Q at plaintext 1, so SEIFERT requires one additional word correction in each witness there. The combined edited cost is 3 substitutions versus 1 unavoidable observed-source conflict; the extra 2 are contextual name repairs.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov12-arrival-departure-and-car-parallel-source-evidence-and-its-limits"></a>

### Parallel source evidence and its limits

The [earlier p174 B/E edition](168.md#edition-cases-radio-seifert) already presents the arrival-enquiry and departure wording. The [frozen parallel-witness snapshot](../../experiments/nov12_arrival_departure_and_car/parallel_witnesses.json) and the new certificate preserve those earlier transcriptions, while the [reviewed p174 image](../../experiments/nov12_arrival_departure_and_car/sources/p174_parallel.png) is independently bound to the original PDF.

| Comparison | Complete observed pairs supporting the edited target | Minimum combined observed-coordinate conflict cost | Combined edited substitutions | Combined printed-mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| p174 B / p183 B arrival enquiry | 37 / 37 | 0 | 0 | 9 |
| p174 E / p183 C departure report | 22 / 23 | 1 | 3 | 0 |

In the first pair, p174 B supplies every one of the eight invalid-glyph values in p183 B. Conversely, p183 B supplies an observed **D at source 20**, which gives **N at plaintext 22** in `EINGETROFFEN`, formerly unresolved in the conservative p174 transcription. Every complete target pair occurs in at least one witness. This is positive source evidence for that letter, beyond a plausible German completion. It does not make the nine individual printed masks disappear from the two diplomatic transcriptions.

The old p174 glyph remains C-like or a defective G. Under its explicitly retained G reading, selecting the D supplied by p183 costs one observed-coordinate substitution in that branch. The source comparison does not claim to change what the older glyph looks like.

In the departure pair, p183 C supports the second E of SEIFERT through **source 2 X**, where p174 E has G. The first E still corresponds to the same **source 28 G** in both witnesses and therefore needs one contextual G→X proposal in each. Thus the complete name costs three substitutions jointly, two more than the unavoidable single observed-source conflict. The joint source support does not turn this shared spelling repair into a direct reading.

The literal interception and originating times differ between the parallel records and remain in their headers. These are additional physical witnesses, not four newly discovered message contents or a claim of first historical decipherment.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov12-arrival-departure-and-car-evidence-credit-and-reproduction"></a>

### Evidence, credit and reproduction

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. The arrival-enquiry and departure wording was already presented for p174 B/E in cases/radio/seifert.md. The new p183 witnesses add coordinate support and a separately priced comparison, not a new claim to that wording or extra message groups.

The certificates independently reconstruct column positions and domains, compare them with the cipher implementation, replay every priced change, and check all readable nonseparator labels. Partial readings have one consistent injective square/source-mask completion witness that re-encrypts exactly; those witness choices are not historical identifications. Source images are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/nov12_arrival_departure_and_car/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and exact source-crop pixels.

## p183 D — Parallel car inquiry with a priced extra-coordinate hypothesis

**Edition context:** A parallel car enquiry with an explicit extra-coordinate model.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-car-query-parallel-frame-a-parallel-car-enquiry-with-an-explicit-extra-coordinate-model"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The p183 D source is almost identical to the independently readable car enquiry in p183 E, but it has an extra observed coordinate and one other disagreement. This edition preserves D's native odd-length diagnostic and separately prices a parallel-copy proposal. The wording was already obtained directly from E; D adds another physical witness with explicit limitations.

The unchanged period key retains the credit to George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry's 2017 key list. ## p183 F — An accommodation-area report around Vierset-Barse and Soheit

**Edition context:** A Jaeger division's accommodation area near Huy.

<a id="edition-cases-military-jaeger-accommodation-area-a-jaeger-divisions-accommodation-area-near-huy"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This message reports an accommodation area for a German Jaeger division near Huy. A prewar illustrated guide supplies the spelling **Vierset-Barse**, supporting one correction in its place list. The complete source body matches its advertised 230 slots, with no change to its frame.

<a id="source-p183-f"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-jaeger-accommodation-area-p183-f"></a>

### p183 F

**Source transcription — header:** `F) -- v -- (14.05 p.m., November 12th); 12.10; RICHI-230`

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order, with non-coordinate glyphs masked:**

```text
ANXAOKX1?XZUXDORTX11140XOPXUNTERBRINGUNGSRAUMXDTXJAEGE1XDIVX13?11XMARC?EXSUEDL?HUYXVIERSWTXBARSEXSOHEITXAOKX1?X1XAM
```

**Edited output — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 2 source-mask fills; no insertion, deletion or reordering:**

```text
ANXAOKX1?XZUXDORTX11140XOPXUNTERBRINGUNGSRAUMXDTXJAEGERXDIVX13?11XMARCHEXSUEDLXHUYXVIERSWTXBARSEXSOHEITXAOKX1?X1XAM
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited output:**

> An AOK 1?. Zu dort 11140 OP. Unterbringungsraum DT JAEGER DIV 13?11: MARCHE, SUEDL HUY, VIERSWT, BARSE, SOHEIT. AOK 1? 1 AM.

**Meaning of this earlier layer:** The message reports an accommodation area for a German Jaeger division, followed by a partially unresolved label and a list of place-like fields. SUEDL HUY means south of Huy. This layer preserves VIERSWT, BARSE and the three unresolved numeral positions; the place-name correction and shared digits are presented separately above.

**Editorial limits:**

- The native body has all 230 printed slots, including two printed dashes in XF--F. No source coordinate is inserted, excluded or reordered.
- The single observed-coordinate proposal JAEGE1 to JAEGER is priced. The two dash fills propose MARC?E to MARCHE and SUEDL?HUY to SUEDLXHUY. These supply readable words and a separator without changing the key.
- VIERSWT and SOHEIT remain literal in this earlier layer. The Vierset proposal above carries its additional substitution explicitly.
- The unknown at plaintext index 8 in the opening AOK1? and at 62 in 13?11 comes from the same fully observed GF square cell. Those two occurrences must take the same digit from {5,6,7,8,9}.
- The final AOK1? unknown at plaintext index 109 is a different fully observed XG square cell and must take a different member of {5,6,7,8,9}. No choice is made merely to make the two AOK labels agree.
- The header retains the literal 14.05 p.m. and 12.10. Neither is used to resolve the date-like or reference labels inside the body.

<a id="edition-cases-military-jaeger-accommodation-area-vierset-barse-in-the-accommodation-list"></a>

### Vierset-Barse in the accommodation list

The received `VIERSWT X BARSE` is proposed as **VIERSET X BARSE**. A plate in
*Huy-pittoresque*, dated about 1885–1890 by the Rijksmuseum, prints the caption
**CHATEAU DE VIERSET-BARSE**. The two fields can therefore be read together as
the place-name **Vierset-Barse**. The intervening X remains the transmitted
separator; the hyphen belongs to the readable display.

The correction costs **one additional observed substitution**, source **170 D→X**.
It changes plaintext position 88 from W to E (`VD→VX`) and leaves the other
114 labels untouched. Including the earlier JAEGER repair and two dash fills,
this place-name layer costs **two substitutions and two source-mask fills**.
It adds no fixed positions: the corrected letter was already a known W.

**Readable German — place-name correction, with the published partial square:**

> An AOK 1?. Zu dort 11140 OP. Unterbringungsraum DT JAEGER DIV 13?11: MARCHE, SUEDL HUY, VIERSET-BARSE, SOHEIT. AOK 1? 1 AM.

<details>
<summary>Exact place-name proposal</summary>

**Edited output — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 2 source-mask fills:**

```text
ANXAOKX1?XZUXDORTX11140XOPXUNTERBRINGUNGSRAUMXDTXJAEGERXDIVX13?11XMARCHEXSUEDLXHUYXVIERSETXBARSEXSOHEITXAOKX1?X1XAM
```

</details>

The [source plate and exact check](../../experiments/p183_vierset_place/README.md)
support this spelling independently of the conditional numeral interpretation
below. MARCHE, SOHEIT and the intermediate reference remain unchanged.

<a id="edition-cases-military-jaeger-accommodation-area-conditional-shared-digits"></a>

### Conditional shared digits

The accommodation report gains **AOK 17** at the opening and **AOK 18** at the close, reaching **115/115 labels** under the shared interpretation. The intermediate field becomes the literal **13711**. Its 7 is coupled to AOK 17 and is not replaced by a separator. The earlier JAEGER repair and two source-mask fills are retained. The [joint reconstruction](../../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> An AOK 17. Zu dort 11140 OP. Unterbringungsraum DT JAEGER DIV 13711: MARCHE, SUEDL HUY, VIERSWT, BARSE, SOHEIT. AOK 18 1 AM.

<details>
<summary>Exact conditional labels</summary>

**Edited output — p183_F, conditional shared square; 115/115 fixed positions:**

```text
ANXAOKX17XZUXDORTX11140XOPXUNTERBRINGUNGSRAUMXDTXJAEGERXDIVX13711XMARCHEXSUEDLXHUYXVIERSWTXBARSEXSOHEITXAOKX18X1XAM
```

</details>
